key_insight: SPARC is a transformer-based model that predicts cancer-related adverse events from longitudinal health measurements, rather than discovering new cancer drugs.
clinical_relevance: Risk predictions could help target supportive care, including G-CSF, to patients most likely to benefit.
method: Pre-trained and fine-tuned on routinely collected longitudinal health measurements.
Evaluated on held-out, prospective, and external cohorts.
Compared pooled multi-institution with single-institution fine-tuning.
evidence_signal: Training used 101,920,379 measurements from 224,047 patients; evaluation included a prospective same-center cohort of 23,126 patients and external cohorts of 26,012, 562,620, and 206,840 patients.
watch_item: Predictive performance does not establish that model-guided care improves outcomes; prospective clinical-impact evaluation remains important.
paper_title: Longitudinal AI Models Predict Cancer Adverse Events
